To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV-1 Gag targeting to plasma membrane and multivesicular body compartments is cell-type dependent and that the late domain in Gag is not required for targeting to the Mvb.

HIV-1 Gag is targeted specifically to the plasma membrane and MVB in HeLa and CD4+ T cells and to the MVB in primary macrophages, and Gag targeting to both cellular locations is important for HIV-1 particle assembly and release.
the targeting and assembly sites of Gag differ in different cell types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of HIV-1 assembly, a process that is critical for virus infectivity.
the targeting of HIV-1 Gag to sites of virus particle assembly.
the molecular mechanism by which HIV-1 assembles into virus particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIV-1 assembly pathway is cell type dependent and involves the plasma membrane and/or the MVB.
the HIV-1 assembly-and-release pathway in human primary macrophages involves a Gag-dependent targeting step and that the MVB is a site of HIV-1 particle assembly.
the HIV-1 assembly-and-release pathway in macrophages is distinct from that in T cells and HeLa cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIV-1 assembly-and-release process can occur in multiple intracellular sites, including the plasma membrane and late endosomes.
Gag targeting and assembly in the plasma membrane and in the MVB is cell type specific.
Gag is transported to the plasma membrane and MVB by two independent mechanisms, and that in the MVB, Gag interacts with a protein that is required for virus assembly and release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the targeting of Gag to the MVB in HIV-1-infected cells is a physiologically important process in virus particle production in primary human macro- phases.
the targeting of HIV-1 Gag to the MVB, which is an endosome-like compartment, is an essential step in HIV-1 assembly in macrophage cells.
the HIV-1 assembly pathway can be cell-type specific and that the MVB may be an alternative site of assembly and particle release in macrophages.
